title: A chord's notes, one at a time

cues.show: You with the guitar, the arpeggio on the neck on screen.
cues.say: An arpeggio is a chord played one note at a time. These dots are the notes of the chord.

cues.show: Point at the ringed notes, tap a few dots.
cues.say: The ringed dots are the root, the note the chord is named after. Tap a dot to hear it.

cues.show: Strum the chord, then press Play to hear the arpeggio.
cues.say: First strum the chord, so the sound is in your ears.

cues.show: Strum the chord, then press Play to hear the arpeggio.
cues.say: Then press Play below to hear the same notes one by one, up and back down.

cues.show: Play the arpeggio on the guitar, slowly.
cues.say: Now play it, from the lowest ringed note up and back down. There are fewer notes on each string than in a scale, so your picking hand jumps strings more often.

cues.show: Play it again, saying the numbers of the notes.
cues.say: Say the numbers as you play: 1, 3, 5. Practice until you find the three notes of the chord without stopping to look for them.

cues.show: Play the notes in another order. Play a scale line that lands on a ringed note.
cues.say: Try things with it. Play the notes in a new order: skip one, come back, repeat one.

cues.show: Play the notes in another order. Play a scale line that lands on a ringed note.
cues.say: Let every note ring into the next, then play them short.

cues.show: Play the notes in another order. Play a scale line that lands on a ringed note.
cues.say: Play a few notes of the scale and land on a note of the arpeggio. Then land on a note that isn't in it, and hear the difference.
